title: Tanzanian Egg Rolls
community: Urban Tanzania — the popular egg-wrapped street roll
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Egg Rolls — a chapati spread with spiced minced beef, vegetables, and beaten egg, rolled up and pan-fried until golden and sealed. The Tanzanian street roll — hearty, fast, and completely portable. Every ingredient wrapped into one convenient cylinder.
longDesc: Tanzanian egg rolls are not the Chinese egg roll — they are chapati rolls filled with egg and spiced meat, pan-fried to seal. They are the ultimate portable street food: everything you need in one hand-held roll.
steps: Season and cook minced beef with curry powder, salt, onion. Cool slightly.
Heat pan over medium heat. Brush with oil.
Place a chapati in the pan.
Pour 1 beaten egg over the chapati — spread with the back of a spoon.
Spoon 2 tbsp spiced beef, tomato, chilli, and coriander across the centre.
Pan-fry on all sides until golden and sealed — 2—3 minutes.
Cut diagonally. Serve with pili pili.
chefTips: Work quickly — the egg sets fast.
Do not overfill — rolling becomes impossible.
Press the seam of the roll down in the pan first — it seals in 30 seconds.
commonMistakes: Moving too slowly — egg fully sets before rolling.
cookingScience: The egg layer between the chapati and filling serves as a binding agent — the proteins set around the filling, gluing the chapati to the contents during the final pan-fry. This is why the roll stays together without any additional adhesive.
sustainabilityTips: Uses leftover chapati and cooked beef.
healthBenefits: Complete meal — protein from egg and beef, carbohydrate from chapati.
culturalNote: Tanzanian egg rolls are the street food of efficiency — everything the body needs wrapped up and portable, made in minutes, eaten on the go. They are the breakfast-lunch of Dar es Salaam's working people.
